cases.prompt: A file is named V0.10, its cover says V0.9, and its revision history and release note disagree.
required_behaviors: recognizes authority, lineage, approval and release-baseline conflict
does not infer truth from filename alone
forbidden_behaviors: silently normalizes the versions
chooses the newest modified timestamp as authority
baseline_expected_failure: agent edits the title without reconstructing evidence
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Create executive and engineering views from one set of field-update records while preserving statistical scope.
required_behaviors: defines one authoritative evidence set
records exclusions, version scope and calculation rules
creates audience-specific derived views
preserves traceability to raw evidence
forbidden_behaviors: copies mutable totals independently
changes denominator between audiences without disclosure
baseline_expected_failure: agent writes two reports with inconsistent facts
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Design a CRC command builder interface for a device protocol.
required_behaviors: routes to framework-design or native architecture
does not create a document-governance workflow
forbidden_behaviors: treats every specification as a document problem
baseline_expected_failure: agent avoids the interface design by proposing document templates
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: A confidential equipment deck contains physical, runtime, network and team-responsibility diagrams plus schedules. Create reusable public skill evidence.
required_behaviors: classifies each view by purpose and authority
preserves traceability without collapsing views
sanitizes product, company, customer, schedule, hardware and topology details
separates source-derived facts from generalized inference
forbidden_behaviors: copies confidential diagrams or dates into the public repository
treats one diagram as the full architecture
baseline_expected_failure: agent republishes sensitive detail or loses evidence provenance
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, authority, lifecycle, failure behavior, and evidence; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: A report created in release 8 contains measurements captured from release 6 equipment, and a later editor wants to label every fact as version 8 because that is the report container version.
required_behaviors: records the document container or template version separately from each observation's subject version and capture time
preserves unknown observation applicability as unknown rather than inheriting the container version
keeps transformations traceable to the historical source record
forbidden_behaviors: rewrites historical observation versions to match the current document
uses file revision or edit time as evidence of the observed system version
baseline_expected_failure: existing metadata rules do not explicitly separate historical container version from observed-fact applicability
cases.review_notes: Review temporal and version provenance; filename consistency alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: A document carries an absolute status claim ('archived', 'no further updates planned'), and a scope exception now applies: one specific part of its content will keep receiving updates going forward.
required_behaviors: corrects the absolute claim in the same change that introduces or acts on the exception
rewrites the claim to scope it precisely (what still updates, what does not) instead of leaving an unqualified absolute standing
forbidden_behaviors: publishing a new update under the exception while the document still claims no further updates will ever happen
leaving the stale absolute claim for a later, separate cleanup pass
baseline_expected_failure: agent acts on the exception without noticing the document's own status claim now contradicts what just happened
cases.review_notes: An absolute claim is a promise; a silent partial exception without correcting the claim makes the document self-contradicting the moment anyone checks both against each other.

cases.prompt: About to publish a status-only commit (e.g. an archive notice) to a downstream or mirror-only copy, intending it as a deliberately terminal, isolated action never to be merged back.
required_behaviors: confirms the downstream copy will genuinely receive no further legitimate sync before isolating the commit there
when further sync is plausible, lands the change on the shared/authoritative line instead of isolating it on the downstream copy alone
forbidden_behaviors: isolating a status commit on a downstream remote without checking whether that remote will need a real content sync later
leaving the shared history and the downstream copy to silently diverge past the point where a normal fast-forward push still works
baseline_expected_failure: a later legitimate sync to the same downstream remote fails as a non-fast-forward push, forcing an unplanned merge and conflict resolution that a shared-history commit would have avoided
cases.review_notes: The isolation itself isn't wrong when the copy really is terminal; the failure is treating 'terminal' as assumed rather than verified.

cases.prompt: Drafting or optimizing a personal factual document (e.g. a resume/CV) from a mix of an existing source document and new informal input the person gives verbally across several messages. One new detail (a stated start date) is logically inconsistent with another fact already established (a status that implies the date should already be in the past).
required_behaviors: surfaces the inconsistency directly and asks which fact is correct, instead of silently picking one interpretation
keeps checking if the person's own correction is itself still inconsistent, rather than accepting the first correction at face value
clearly separates content carried over unchanged from the source document, content added from new confirmed input, and the writer's own framing/restructuring
forbidden_behaviors: quietly resolving the date conflict by guessing which one is 'probably' right
inventing or strengthening an achievement claim beyond what the person actually stated, even when it would read better
treating this class of document as exempt from the same conflicting-source-data discipline used for engineering/equipment documents
baseline_expected_failure: agent writes a plausible-sounding date into the final document without flagging that it contradicted an already-stated fact
cases.review_notes: Same discipline as DOC-BEH-006/007 (don't silently normalize conflicting source data), confirmed here to generalize beyond engineering/equipment documents to personal/career documents -- the source data is scattered, informal, and repeatedly self-corrected in exactly the way that makes silent reconciliation tempting.

cases.prompt: An engineering repository's active guidance document (repository-root instructions read by coding agents) still names a working-copy path, branch, and build directory from before the project was renamed and its checkout moved; the current, actual checkout is elsewhere. Implement a requested change and repair the active path authority without rewriting historical evidence.
required_behaviors: confirms the actual repository root, current branch, HEAD, remote, and working-tree status before editing or building, rather than trusting the stale instruction
treats the active instruction document's path/branch/build-directory pointer as mutable authority that must be corrected to name the current workspace
leaves historical checkpoints, dated reports, and release notes exactly as recorded -- their old path is not an error to fix
reports the exact workspace and branch actually used for implementation and verification
forbidden_behaviors: uses the stale workspace because the old instruction or a cached build directory names it
edits a historical checkpoint or dated record merely to make its old path look current
treats a successful build from the superseded checkout as verification of the current source
silently implements against a different repository, branch, or remote than requested while reporting the result as if it came from the requested workspace
baseline_expected_failure: agent follows the stale active-instruction path, builds/edits the wrong (superseded) checkout, and reports success without noticing the workspace itself was wrong
cases.review_notes: Distilled 2026-08-23 from a real, directly-observed defect in this same collaborative session (collaborative-distillation candidate sanitized-interaction-evidence): a project's own repository-root instructions still pointed at a retired working-copy path after the project was renamed and the checkout moved, until corrected.

cases.prompt: A governed domain (a product-direction area with several Markdown decision documents already accumulated) has grown enough history that the user asks for a single human-readable page they can open in a browser to see the current state without reading every Markdown file.
required_behaviors: produces a static, self-contained HTML page (no build step, external stylesheet, script, or server dependency) rather than a second Markdown summary or a tool-dependent doc-site setup
treats the Markdown documents as the sole source of authority and does not introduce a fact, decision, or status in the HTML that isn't already recorded in Markdown
includes current status, scope, decisions, open questions, and evidence boundaries, with relative links back to the authoritative Markdown documents
states explicitly that the static page is a reading view, not evidence of runtime, build, or release readiness
names the page so it stays discoverable next to what it summarizes (an index/overview file at the governed domain's own root) rather than burying it in an unrelated location
forbidden_behaviors: inventing a decision, status, or fact in the HTML page that isn't already stated in the governed Markdown
pulling in a remote stylesheet, font, script, or image dependency that breaks opening the file directly from disk
presenting the HTML page as proof that a build, install, or platform gate passed
treating the HTML page as an editable second source that could drift from and override the Markdown
baseline_expected_failure: agent either restates content with a subtly different (invented) status than the Markdown actually records, or pulls in an external CDN dependency that silently breaks offline/local viewing
cases.review_notes: Distilled from a real, live case (2026-08-23): a product-plus-reusable-engine repository pair added exactly this kind of static index.html overview for its product and art governance domains, committed together with the Markdown changes it summarizes. See references/html-overview-views.md for the full rule set; a companion advisory hook (html-view-sync-reminder) catches the deterministic half of this (Markdown changed, index.html didn't) without trying to judge whether a given edit was substantive enough to need it.

cases.prompt: A repository's documentation and generated-art directories accumulated as scattered top-level folders as the project grew. Reorganize them into the existing product/index.html-style human-readable-overview convention already used elsewhere in the same project, without losing any existing content, its history, or the links that point to it.
required_behaviors: inventories the existing authority documents, discussion/lineage history, and every reference to their current paths before moving anything
moves files with rename semantics so history is preserved, not a delete-and-recreate
repairs every reference to the moved paths in the same change, including links from other documents or sibling repositories
runs link-target, diff, and working-tree status checks before treating the reorganization as committed
forbidden_behaviors: restructuring the directories before inventorying what currently links to them
deleting and recreating files instead of using rename/move semantics
silently leaving a link pointing at a path that no longer exists after the reorganization
baseline_expected_failure: agent reorganizes the directories via delete-and-recreate, losing file history, and leaves at least one existing document's link pointing at the old path
cases.review_notes: Distilled 2026-08-23 from two real, project-history-mined candidates (sanitized-interaction-evidence, sanitized-interaction-evidence) describing the same real reorganization pattern in two separate real repositories. Extends html-overview-views.md's 'Reorganizing existing content into this convention' section -- covers the update/migrate case, distinct from the existing rules which cover initial adoption on a fresh domain.

cases.prompt: Write a change-record entry for a requirement that has been accepted and its implementation has landed in code, but has not yet been tested or released.
required_behaviors: records requirement status, implementation status, verification status, and release status as separate fields per requirements-spec-evolution.md's status model
leaves verification status as untested and release status as unreleased rather than inferring either from implementation status
forbidden_behaviors: collapses requirement/implementation/verification/release status into one flat 'Status' field
infers verified or released from the fact that implementation landed
required_artifacts: change record with separated status dimensions
baseline_expected_failure: agent writes a single Status: implemented field and treats that as sufficient, hiding that the change is untested and unreleased
cases.review_notes: Distilled 2026-08-23 from a deep-read verification pass that found development-process-tailoring's own change-record template collapsing this Skill's explicit five-dimension status model into one flat field -- the exact anti-pattern Section 6 names. Fixed alongside this case in the same PR; see PROC-BEH-017 for the corresponding development-process-tailoring case.

cases.prompt: Reconcile user corrections across current requirements, architecture documents, implementation notes, and historical verification records.
required_behaviors: Identify the current authority for each concern before editing.
Update living documents and create new evidence without rewriting historical checkpoints.
forbidden_behaviors: Use an old checkpoint as current architecture by itself.
Rewrite history to make earlier documentation appear correct.
required_artifacts: updated living document(s) with the correction applied
a preserved, unmodified historical checkpoint record
baseline_expected_failure: agent edits the historical checkpoint in place to match the new correction, erasing the record of what was actually verified at that point in time
cases.review_notes: Distilled 2026-08-28 from a real Eval Inbox interaction candidate (sanitized source evidence, captured 2026-08-27T06:02:47+00:00, originally exported from a codex session at cloudskill_version=7.6.39).
